compile.nuance: Catch-all bundle: 7 defect options span 3 check_types (scripted_review x3 income-fairness/discriminatory-practice judgment, date_window x3 Reg B notice-timing, doc_completeness x1 notice content). Only the income-treatment options (alimony/child-support, part-time/pension/annuity/retirement) have precise Selling Guide sections (B3-3.4-02, B3-3.4-03; note 'part time income' itself is not named anywhere in the 390-section corpus -- only the pension/annuity/retirement half of that option is covered). The three date_window notice-timing options (30-day action notice, 90-day counteroffer notice, 30-day NOI) and the doc_completeness notice-content option are Regulation B (12 CFR 1002) mechanics that live outside the Fannie Selling Guide; A3-2-01 only carries the general 'must comply with ECOA' obligation, not the granular timing/content rules. Decomposition required to split into children with correctly scoped (including non-guide/external Reg B) citations.

finding.description: There is evidence of use of assumptions or aggregate statistics relating to the likelihood that an applicant(s) will bear or rear children as part of the evaluation of credit.

defect_options.response: The UW evaluated married and unmarried applicants by different standards

finding.description: The file evidences that unmarried applicants were evaluated by the same standards as married applicants and not treated differently as a result of their of marital status.

defect_options.response: The UW may have considered race, color, religion, national origin or sex in evaluating an applicant

finding.description: There is evidence that race, color, national origin, religion, marital status, sex, age, the receipt of public assistance income, or the exercise of rights under the Consumer Credit Protection Act were utilized in the evaluation of credit.

compile.nuance: Single citation only: A3-2-01 is the Selling Guide's sole reference to ECOA's anti-discrimination provisions (repurchase-remedy context); it states the general compliance obligation but does not itself enumerate the specific prohibited-basis/subjective-standard/childbearing-assumption doctrine tested by these 4 options -- that doctrine is native to Reg B/ECOA case law, not the Selling Guide. No second Selling Guide section was found (grep of 'discriminat' across all 390 sections surfaced only appraisal-bias sections B4-1.1-02/-04 and A3-2-01, none on file-level underwriting-decision fair lending).
